title: JPMorganChase says vendors that serve it were hit by a cyberattack; marketing data may be exposed
action: Chase customers: expect phishing that uses your name and email address, and do not follow links in unexpected messages; sign in through the official app or site.
date_note: Date of the bank's statement, as reported; the attack date is not stated.
exec: A major US bank says attackers reached marketing data at its service providers, a reminder that vendor breaches expose customer contact details.
impact: JPMorganChase says attackers may have accessed some customer names and email addresses held by the vendors. No numbers are given.
plain: JPMorganChase says companies that provide services to the bank were attacked, and that marketing data, possibly including some customers' names and email addresses, may have been accessed. The bank says its services are not disrupted.
summary: JPMorganChase said on Thursday that third parties providing services to the bank were the target of a cyberattack. Based on its investigation so far, the bank believes attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses. It says there is no disruption to its services. No attacker is named.

validation.note: ABC13 quotes the bank's own statement; The Sun page could not be read and the Independent link was not opened. No link to the bank's statement was found.

review.note: Compared bank statement wording (vendors targeted, marketing data, may include names and emails, no disruption), no numbers, no attacker, date against ABC13
